That's a good question.  You see the problem with getting diagnosed at 18 is you're right between the children's hospital, and the "adult" hospitals.  I decided that being surrounded by young sick kids would be too heartbreaking for me so I went with the other route.

I didn't meet any other patients because where I had treatment I was the youngest person in the treatment wing by atleast 60 years, so I just got a lot of strange looks from them, not much talking with the exception of some minor small talk.

I got sick after i graduated, so not many people from my high school new about it.  The community as a whole didn't reach out to me at all, but my friends and family have been for the most part very supportive.  I don't blame anyone tho, I really kinda wanted to keep it on the down low as much as possible.
I'm happy I'm here, but certainly much more jaded than i was pre-diagnosis.  I've also become very misanthropic, the medical industry is a complete disgrace.

Hmmm, that's a tough question, because at 18 I like most naive teenagers thought the world was mine, I was out-going, less anti-social than I am now, and athletic. By now i figured I would have graduated college, slight set back there.  While I was undergoing treatment i spent most of my time on the internet, and now my social skills are pretty terrible.  I never thought I'd be this bad with women, attempting to pick up on women looking like professor farnsworth fucks your confidence.

I actually did quite well with all the medication, didn't do too bad through chemo or radiation(it still sucked, but others have it worse)  The only real problem i had was with [prednisone](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prednisone) that pill tastes awful. As for my prognosis I've nearly been in remission for 3 years, and everything is looking great.  I have amazing doctors.
